Allah Janre Sain Zainab Ne Kiwein Qaid Nibhai.
Kiwein Safar Kitay Baaj Bhirawaan Haye Dard Satai.

1
Abid Nu Pathran De Wich Kadi Safraan Che Sakina Nu Kadi Bhaina Nu.
Qaidi Hathaan De Nal Sanbhdi Reh Gayi Zahra Di Kamai.
Apnre Hi Ghar De Wich Jis Dam Abdullah Ne Puchiya Keh Tu Bibi Koan Aye.
Bas Ronde Hoyaan Khak Utha Ke Zainab Ne Urai.

2
Zalim De Zabaan Utay Aaya Jadoon Naa Fatima Zahra Da Bhare Majmay Wich.
Maa Di Azmat Layi Khutbe Parhdi Dhi Zahra Di Aayi.
Amari De Naal Mil Ke Jiwein Rondi Aye Koi Dhi Owein Zainab Roi.
Jadoon Maa Di Rida Waqt-e-Rehai Gal Sain Ne Lai.

3
Jad V Soraj Saweray Charhda Si Aap Jhuk Jandi Si Wich Haal-e-Raku De Zainab.
Aynj Balaan Utay Rayi Chawaan Kardi Haye Zahra Di Jayi.
Aaj V Saqlain Janab-e-Mehdi Onna Rawaan Taun Hataonde Odde Pairaan De Nishaan.
Jinaa Rawaan Utay Shamiyaa Zainab Kal Qaidi Turai

/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
p = Path('src/data/lyrics/allah-janre-sain-zainab-ne-kiwein-qaid-lyrics-2018-tajpoints-2fc397dd25cadc266a92.md')
header, rest = p.read_text().split('romanLyrics: |-\\n', 1)
roman, body = rest.split('\\n---\\n', 1)
names = {'Allah', 'Zainab', 'Abid', 'Sakina', 'Zahra', 'Abdullah', 'Fatima', 'Saqlain', 'Shamiyaa'}
def sentence(line):
    words = line.split()
    if not words or words[0].isdigit():
        return line
    return '  ' + ' '.join(word if i == 0 or word in names else 'janab-e-Mehdi' if word == 'Janab-e-Mehdi' else word.lower() for i, word in enumerate(words))
updated = '\\n'.join(map(sentence, roman.splitlines()))
assert updated.lower() == roman.lower()
assert [len(block.splitlines()) for block in updated.split('\\n\\n')] == [len(block.splitlines()) for block in body.strip().split('\\n\\n')] == [2, 5, 5, 5]
p.write_text(header + 'romanLyrics: |-\\n' + updated + '\\n---\\n' + body)
PY"

item.text: Reconstructed all 14 verses in Shahmukhi Punjabi and verified that they align line for line with the preserved Roman wording in `romanLyrics`. The verses use Punjabi grammar, so I updated the language metadata to `Panjabi`, `pa-Arab`, and `rtl`. I rendered the ambiguous `Janre` as `جانڑے` in the opening verse and kept the title’s distinct `Janay` reading as `جانے`.
